## Overview

This example uses a small, reproducible dataset to demonstrate a typical data
science report workflow: prepare data, summarize it, and communicate a result.
Replace the example values and analysis with your own.

## Data and analysis

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the example measurements"

import pandas as pd

measurements = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "group": ["A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B"],
        "value": [12, 15, 14, 18, 17, 20],
    }
)

summary = measurements.groupby("group", as_index=False)["value"].agg(
    count="count",
    mean="mean",
)
summary
```

The mean measurement is higher in group B in this example. The sample is
intentionally small and illustrative; it does not support broader conclusions.

## Visualization

```{python}
#| label: fig-measurements
#| fig-cap: "Measurements by group"

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

measurements.boxplot(column="value", by="group")
plt.title("Measurements by group")
plt.suptitle("")
plt.xlabel("Group")
plt.ylabel("Measurement")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
